target.title: test(plugins): cover manifest tool-availability gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.ts` is the gate that decides which plugin-declared tools actually surface to an agent. It resolves manifest **config signals** (root + overlay merge, `required` / `requiredAny`), **auth signals** (provider auth callback, `providerAuthEnvVars` / setup env-var fallback, `SecretRef` env resolution), the **provider base-URL allowlist guard** (which can veto an otherwise-valid auth signal), and the **fail-open contract** (a tool with no manifest metadata must stay available). This module shipped with no direct coverage, so a regression in any of these gates — for example hiding an unannotated tool, or dropping the base-URL allowlist veto that keeps a tool from reaching an off-allowlist proxy — would not be caught before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change is coverage-only: it adds `src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.test.ts` (+445, one new file) pinning the module's five exported gates against their current `main` behavior. No production code is touched. Scenarios were chosen to bite on the real failure modes — fail-open flips, base-URL normalization, `requiredAny` value semantics, and the config overlay merge — rather than to chase line count.

**Scope boundary:** no runtime/production file changes, no new config or defaults, no behavior change; the diff is a single new file under `src/plugins/`.

## User Impact

No user-visible or runtime change. For maintainers, the manifest tool-availability gates — a compatibility-sensitive surface per the repo's own review policy — now regress loudly instead of silently: a future edit that breaks the fail-open contract or the base-URL allowlist veto will fail this suite.

## Evidence

Linux (Node 22.22), `pnpm install` from source, rebased onto current `main` (`98ca8c94`). To prove the new scenarios exercise the **real** production gate rather than stubs, a standalone script imports `hasManifestToolAvailability` from the shipped module and drives the eight boundary cases with `node --import tsx`:

```text
$ node --import tsx drive-mta.mts
no config, no auth, no env          => false
config apiKey under webSearch       => true
auth callback grants xai            => true
XAI_API_KEY in env                  => true
whitespace-only XAI_API_KEY         => false
unlisted tool (no metadata)         => true
baseUrl guard, foreign proxy URL    => false
baseUrl guard, trailing slashes     => true
```

Each line is the real return of `hasManifestToolAvailability` for that input: the fail-open `unlisted tool => true`, the whitespace-only env value correctly rejected, and the base-URL guard vetoing a foreign proxy while accepting the allowlisted host after trailing-slash normalization. Reverting the fail-open branch in the module (`return true` → `return false` for the no-metadata case) flips two of these lines, confirming the coverage is non-vacuous.

**Related:** none — coverage mined from the module itself; no linked issue.
